craft_notes: Sthāyin: āṇava rung — low-means dignity. Sanskrit-first: bahudhā kept as opening breadth (many-mouthed). Rows: 3 (interval-penetration as slipping). Close: rest waits. Rejected: glorifying the low way — killed: optative commands, not praises. Read aloud: coaxing cadence — breadth narrows to rest.

lines: Many-mouthed, the low way still aims at Śiva;
slip into its seams and rest where the near station waits.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yadetadbahudhā proktamāṇavaṃ śivatāptaye | tatrāntarantarāviśya viśrāmyetsavidhe pade

reads_against.argmap: The manifold āṇava works through its intervals and proximate rest.
c1_essence: The manifold-taught āṇava aims at Śiva-hood; penetration of its intervals, rest in the proximate station.
